thread:
incident-bot: PAGERS: High error rate and cross-region latency spike detected for routing-policy service (alert id: rout-9832). Affected: eu-west2 -> ap-south1; increased 5xxs and >2s tail latency for cross-region routed requests. Pager: sres-oncall.

maya: saw this pop up ~30s ago, looks like a sudden jump in cross-region RTTs and a wave of 5xxs from traffic that should have stayed in eu-west2.

oliver: confirmed. Grafana: regional-steer latency SLO breach for eu-west2. Screenshot: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/steer/xxxxx (link).

samir: traffic graph shows a subset of requests being routed to ap-south1 instead of eu-west2 (policy eval shows eu->ap weight flip on some keys). Not consistent across routers.

jessica: is this the same as the policy rollout from last night? We had the new latency-based routing tweak merged.

maya: yes, we deployed the algo tweak at 03:12 UTC. Canary looked fine but looks like under certain probe patterns the policy table gets an inconsistent backfill and flips region pinning for ~2-3% of hashes.

anita: paging owners: @samir (routing infra) and @maya (sre). Product notified: @product-oncall.

product-oncall: flagged by a handful of customers in EU complaining about increased latency. No support tickets yet, but we've seen traces with 500+ms extra RTT.

samir: first action: pause the new latency-based weight adjustments across control-plane. Running rollback job now: `kubectl -n routing exec job/weight-sync -- curl -X POST /v1/weights/rollback`

incident-bot: Action scheduled: rollback job started by samir at 1778901265.

maya: oncall, can you start a targeted pin for eu-west2 for traffic from the affected prefixes while rollback completes? That should cut the customer impact.

oliver: attempting temporary override: `redwoodctl routing override create --scope region --region eu-west2 --selector estate:public --ttl 120`

anita: confirm override applied on edge cluster eu-west2-a and eu-west2-b.

jessica: monitoring traces now — p50 looks back to normal, p95 dropping. Some clients still show ap-south1 hits due to DNS cache and persistent connections.

maya: can we invalidate caches? Plan: (1) Rollback weight tweak (in progress), (2) pin eu-west2 for 2 min TTL, (3) send edge command to drain existing sticky connections that have been pinned to ap-south1, (4) monitor 5xxs and latencies.

samir: rollback finished at 1778901310, control-plane version back to stable.

incident-bot: rollback job completed successfully.

oliver: initiating connection drain: `redwoodctl edge connection drain --region ap-south1 --selector misrouted=true` — started.

anita: also posting a short BGP announcement change to prefer eu-west2 egress for our proxy network (low-risk, small pref tweak).

product-oncall: ETA for customer-visible improvement?

maya: p50 should be immediate for newly routed requests (~30-60s). p95 will take DNS TTL and active connections: estimate 4-8 minutes to be back to baseline for most customers.

jessica: we are seeing error rate drop from 3.8% -> 1.1% in last 120s. Latency tail improving.

samir: note: discovered a race in policy backfill where concurrent weight writes could set an older shard state over a newer one when derived metrics arrived late. Root cause path: metric ingestion latency + eventual consistency window.

oliver: filing short mitigation blurb for status page: "Intermittent cross-region routing anomaly affecting a subset of EU traffic; temporary override and rollback applied; mitigation in progress."

anita: status page draft done — please +1: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/xxxxx

maya: +1. Also capturing affected customers list: looked up top 10 customer prefixes — 4 customers had >10% of their requests misrouted, we'll surface with support.

product-oncall: opening an incident ticket to CS for outreach to those 4 customers.

incident-bot: ACTION: oncall handoff due in 30m: maya -> next-oncall (standard).

samir: quick post-check: we've added a short-lived write-lock to weight-sync to prevent concurrent backfills until we push a proper fix. Patching now: branch `fix/weight-backfill-race`.

jessica: telemetry capture: saving full traces and logs for timeframe 1778901200-1778901400. Archiving to s3: s3://incidents/1778901234/traces.tar.gz

oliver: residuals: ~0.2% of traffic still hitting ap-south1 due to clients with long-lived TCP connections — we'll keep draining for another 10m.

maya: current status: rollback + pin + drains in place; customer-visible impact falling; next steps: code fix on routing control-plane (samir), expanded replay tests, and postmortem within 48h.

anita: assigning follow-ups: `INC-177890` created with tasks: outreach, telemetry retention (30d), patch, expanded integration test.

product-oncall: thanks team. I'll coordinate communications and customer outreach. Will update when CS reaches affected customers.

samir: pushing hotfix PR, will request review in 10m.

maya: standing down page rotation in 20m if metrics stay stable; if not, we escalate to SEV.

incident-bot: Incident updated: mitigation applied, monitoring. Severity: SEV-2 -> under monitoring.

oliver: thumbs for postmortem — include checklist items for canary probing and stronger backfill locks.

jessica: copying logs to the SOC and compliance bucket for audit.

maya: thanks all. Filing final incident thread notes after metrics hold.

product-oncall: tagging for follow-up: @samir @jessica @anita @oliver
